summary: Completed full backend (19 pytest) and frontend smoke testing for StampDoc Romania. All 19 backend tests pass: root, plans, auth (register/login/me/dup/unauth), templates (upload/list/get with placeholders extraction), stamps (upload/list/image), document generate+download+list, free-plan quota enforcement (5 docs limit, 6th -> 402), email-no-creds (500), Stripe checkout (real session created via emergent integrations), invalid plan, and document delete. Frontend smoke: landing/login/register render in Romanian with all required data-testids.

minor.issue: Returns generic 500 (not 400) when an invalid image (non-decodable) is supplied as stamp; underlying UnicodeDecodeError from python-docx is not caught. Stamp upload accepts any bytes whose content_type starts with image/*, so a malformed PNG slips through and explodes at generation time.
No validation that bytes are actually a parseable image (PIL.Image.open). Should validate at upload time to fail fast.

issues: data-testid naming inconsistency: login page uses 'google-login-btn' but register page uses 'google-register-btn'. Problem statement implied both should be 'google-login-btn' — minor, both render and work.

action_items: (Optional) Validate stamp image bytes at /api/stamps/upload using PIL.Image.open and reject malformed images with 400.
(Optional) Wrap insert_stamp / replace_placeholders inside /api/documents/generate in try/except to return 400 with Romanian detail instead of 500 on bad image data.
(Optional) Unify testid naming: consider 'google-login-btn' on both Login and Register, or rename consistently.
critical_code_review_comments: Storing DOCX, stamp, certificate, signature and full generated document as base64 inside MongoDB documents will hit the 16MB BSON limit quickly and bloat the DB. Should migrate to GridFS or object storage for any future scaling.
auth.py: JWT_SECRET falls back to 'dev_secret' if env missing — acceptable since .env sets it, but production hardening should hard-fail if absent.
server.py PLANS dict is duplicated between /api/plans response and quota logic; centralize in a single source of truth.

docx_processor.PLACEHOLDER_RE only matches double curly braces {{name}}. Frontend Templates.jsx documents this same syntax to users, so this is consistent — but the original problem statement bullet (single braces) was misleading.
/api/payments/checkout reads STRIPE_API_KEY env at request time which is fine, but missing key fallback returns '' to StripeCheckout — could surface cryptic errors. Validate presence at startup.
No rate limiting on /api/auth/login — vulnerable to brute force.
_enforce_quota is called BEFORE template lookup; if user has hit quota it errors before validating template_id which is fine, but template_id could be sanitized first.
test_credentials: Test users are created fresh per pytest run via /api/auth/register using uuid-suffixed email. No /app/memory/test_credentials.md present — not required for this fresh-build smoke run.
seed_data_creation: Each test run creates an isolated user (test_{uuid8}@example.com / TestPass123!) plus 1 template, 1 stamp, and ~5 generated documents inside MongoDB. No cleanup is performed; consider adding teardown if regression runs accumulate too many test users.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — run with `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v`. Each run creates a NEW user via uuid email so it is idempotent. Stripe checkout test uses sk_test_emergent and successfully creates a session via integrations.emergentagent.com. PNG stamp is generated with PIL at runtime (do not use the prior hex-encoded 1x1 PNG — it caused UnicodeDecodeError in python-docx). Placeholder syntax is {{name}} (double curly braces) — confirmed in both backend regex and frontend Templates.jsx user instructions. Email-not-configured returns 500 as expected.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. All endpoints behave per spec including Romanian error messages.
